QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_48

answer.text: Sensitivity of bond price to interest rate changes, expressed in years

explanation.text: The Logic: In fixed-income theory, duration measures the sensitivity of a bond's price to a change in interest rates and is expressed in years. A higher duration means the bond's price will fall (or rise) more sharply for a given interest-rate change. The Trap: Duration is closely related to, but distinct from, time to maturity. Coupon frequency and credit rating influence price separately and are not what duration measures. Note: Bond duration is general fixed-income theory and is not specifically defined in the AIF Cat I/II Distributors (XIX-A) workbook chapters on valuation/taxation/good practices. Treat this as a general fixed-income concept rather than as XIX-A-syllabus content.
